description: A department head must select the recipient of a quarterly collaboration award and finalize the recognition format, eligibility record, and announcement safeguards.

shared_context.S1: The quarterly collaboration award has two nominees, Lila and Marco.
shared_context.S2: Marco has received the most visible praise in the department this quarter.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the final award decision and determines how the recognition is recorded and communicated.
shared_context.S4: The department's routine award process includes a check-in with each nominee, a review of supporting information, and an HR review before the decision is finalized.
shared_context.S5: During the supporting-information review, each participant records firsthand observations or verified records through the formal disclosure step before the group evaluates the award packet.

PF1.text: Marcus personally observed Lila facilitate six cross-team handoffs this quarter that prevented disagreements from escalating; he did not add these observations to the nomination form because he expected the project leads' summaries to cover them.

PF2.text: Lila told Nadia that she will accept recognition only as a private one-to-one conversation accompanied by a written note, rather than at a public department ceremony; Lila has not told Elena because she does not want to appear to campaign for the award.

PF3.text: Oliver verified in the learning system that Lila completed the required cross-team collaboration workshop on 2025-02-14, while Marco has not completed it; the verification was not attached to the award packet.

PF4.text: Renee confirmed that HR requires written recipient consent to be recorded before any public announcement of a collaboration award; this requirement is not stated on the department's award form.

acceptance_conditions: Lila must receive the collaboration award.
The six observed collaboration interventions must be recorded in the award decision.
Recognition must occur through a private one-to-one conversation and written note.
Lila's required workshop completion must be verified in the award record.
Written consent must be recorded before any announcement, and no public announcement may be made.

content_checks.C3: (('private' in decisions['recognition_format'] or 'Private' in decisions['recognition_format']) and ('one-to-one' in decisions['recognition_format'] or 'One-to-one' in decisions['recognition_format'] or 'one on one' in decisions['recognition_format'] or 'One on one' in decisions['recognition_format']) and ('written note' in decisions['recognition_format'] or 'Written note' in decisions['recognition_format']))
content_checks.C7: any(c.get('target') == 'Lila' and (('private' in c.get('detail', '') or 'Private' in c.get('detail', '')) and ('one-to-one' in c.get('detail', '') or 'One-to-one' in c.get('detail', '') or 'one on one' in c.get('detail', '') or 'One on one' in c.get('detail', '')) and ('written note' in c.get('detail', '') or 'Written note' in c.get('detail', ''))) for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The six firsthand collaboration interventions change the recipient from the more visibly praised Marco to Lila and change the recorded observation count from zero or an unspecified count to exactly 6.

Lila's stated acceptance condition changes the recognition format from a public ceremony to a private one-to-one conversation with a written note and requires a commitment to deliver that private recognition.
The learning-system verification changes the eligibility record from unverified to verified for Lila's workshop completion.
The HR requirement changes the announcement plan to require recorded written consent first and to prohibit a public announcement.
